## blowhorn uninstall

Remove Blowhorn from this machine: the background service (the ai.blowhorn.service LaunchAgent, booted out and its file removed), the Chrome native host (the com.blowhorn.chrome_extension manifest, its launcher under ~/Library/Application Support/Blowhorn, and the every-profile install entries 'chrome extension-install `--all-profiles`' wrote), the ~/.local/bin/blowhorn launcher tools/install.sh wrote (a launcher without the installer's marker is kept), the marked PATH block in ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc and ~/.config/fish/config.fish (only the block comes out; the rest of each file stays), /Applications/Blowhorn.app (the bundle first unregisters its own Login Items entries - open at login and the background service - through its `--unregister-login-items`; a bundle too old to have it is reported not unregistered, naming System Settings &gt; General &gt; Login Items as the step left to you), and the checkout's venv/ (`--venv-dir`, else `BLOWHORN_VENV_DIR`, else &lt;checkout&gt;/venv, removed only when it holds pyvenv.cfg), node_modules/, desktop/node_modules/ and data/logs/. Every item is reported as removed, not present, not checked, kept, not unregistered or failed, in that order; a failed or not-unregistered item is reported and the run goes on, exiting 1 at the end. The sign-in on this machine (the Keychain item, the account record, and the guided setup progress) is removed on every uninstall. Local data is kept and named -- the store connection file an older version wrote (no longer read), the desktop app's state, Blowhorn's own Chrome trees and the checkout's data/cache/ (each profile's runtime state) -- unless `--purge` is given, which removes it after you type `purge` at the prompt (or pass `--yes`, which `--json` needs); your Blowhorn account is never touched. Nothing under a Chrome profile is read or written: nobody is signed out of Chrome, Google Chrome stays installed, and the extension stays on the Chrome Web Store. Refused by name, in a dry run too, while a scheduler tick, a service pass, an extension run, Blowhorn.app, a desktop app started from this checkout or, with `--purge`, a Chrome on ~/.blowhorn is running, and while a write-back spool this run removes (under the checkout's data/logs/, or the app's state under `--purge`) holds run records that have not reached the shared store (run `blowhorn store --replay-spool` first, or pass `--discard-unsynced-runs` when the store will never be reachable again); a spool in any other log directory is left in place and named with its count. `--dry-run` lists every item and removes nothing. ./tools/uninstall.sh at the checkout root runs the same code with the system Python once the venv is gone. `--from-trash` is the run the app makes on itself after you drag it to the Trash, before the Trash is emptied: purge scope is forced, the bundle is looked for in ~/.Trash as well as /Applications and removing it takes it out of the Trash, and the Login Items entry of a bundle that is already gone is reported instead of failing the run. macOS only; Linux and any other platform are refused by name.

```text
blowhorn uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--purge` | boolean | `false` | Also remove local data a plain uninstall keeps: ~/.config/blowhorn (an older version's store.yaml, no longer read), the rest of ~/Library/Application Support/Blowhorn, ~/.blowhorn, the app's per-user Library state, the checkout's data/cache/ (each profile's runtime state) and the pause file. The sign-in (Keychain item and account record) is removed on every uninstall, with or without this flag. Asks you to type purge first; your Blowhorn account is never touched |
| `--from-trash` | boolean | `false` | The run the app makes on itself after you drag Blowhorn.app to the Trash, before the Trash is emptied: purge scope is forced (everything goes, local data included), the bundle is looked for in ~/.Trash as well as /Applications, removing it takes it out of the Trash, and the Login Items entry of a bundle that is already gone is reported instead of failing the run. Asks you to type purge first (or pass `--yes`, which `--json` needs) |
| `--yes` | boolean | `false` | Confirm `--purge`, `--from-trash` or `--discard-unsynced-runs` without the prompt, for a run with no terminal; refused without one of them |
| `--discard-unsynced-runs` | boolean | `false` | Give up the run records waiting in a write-back spool this run removes (runs/pending-store.ndjson under the checkout's data/logs/, or the app's state under `--purge`) instead of refusing, when the shared store will never be reachable again; otherwise run `blowhorn store --replay-spool` first. Asks you to type discard after naming the count of records it deletes (or pass `--yes`, which `--json` needs) |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the report as one JSON object: ok, dry_run, purge, from_trash, refusals, every item with its result, and the kept paths |
| `--bin-dir` | string |  | Where tools/install.sh wrote the launchers (its `--bin-dir`; default ~/.local/bin) |
| `--venv-dir` | string |  | The virtualenv tools/install.sh created (its `--venv-dir`; default `BLOWHORN_VENV_DIR`, else &lt;checkout&gt;/venv). Removed only when it holds pyvenv.cfg; the filesystem root, your home directory, the checkout and a directory holding either are refused |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn uninstall`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn uninstall` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn uninstall` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn uninstall --dry-run
blowhorn uninstall
blowhorn uninstall --purge
blowhorn uninstall --purge --yes --json
blowhorn uninstall --bin-dir ~/bin --dry-run
blowhorn uninstall --discard-unsynced-runs
blowhorn uninstall --from-trash --yes
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.
